steps.step: Arrives knowing nothing about ReachKit and, before scrolling, reads what it is and finds the one field ready to type in — with a look at the running product beside it, or just below on a small screen; watches the demo, or reads the page unbroken where there is none; then reads down it why they should care, what it does for them, and what they do to start today
Types their domain into the one field on the landing page, or opens a shared report link — and a scan starts, unless a report for that domain already exists

Waits through a scan that names each stage and returns a readable report inside a minute — or, when the scan stops early, gets back an incomplete report that says what is missing and offers them one re-scan there and then, without waiting out the week a finished report waits; or, when the measurement fails, is told in writing what happened and offered a retry; or, when a limit is met, is told in writing which limit it was and, where there is one to give, when they may scan again
Reads the verdict at the top: one score, its band in words, one written line naming what holds the score down, and a dash with a written line wherever something could not be measured
Reads what AI tells buyers — on how many of their market's biggest searches an AI answer appears, which brands it names instead of them, and the search behind each question

Reads their Google presence — their share of those same searches beside each rival, the biggest searches they are absent from, and the standing line saying every figure here was measured on US Google in English and that more countries are coming

Corrects the category when the report has read their business as the wrong kind of market, and returns to the verdict, the AI answers and the Google presence to read them again against the corrected market
Reads the three problems, copies the free robots fix, and reads the complete method in the DIY sections

Reads what the first page would be — its title, what it targets, who it takes ground from, and how many more were found behind it — and gives their email address as the trade, told before they type what else that address will receive
Receives the finished page in their inbox, and at most three follow-ups afterwards, stopping the moment they subscribe or opt out
Chooses Start ReachKit where the price is offered — their own report, or a price surface with no report behind it — and pays €49, having created no account
Opens the sign-in email that the payment produced and lands on setup
If they stop partway, is asked to come back and finish setup, and picks up where they left off
Settles the site address — confirms or corrects the domain their report measured, or types it in when the purchase had no report behind it

Or, where setup will not accept the address they give, reads one written line saying so that names a way to reach a person and says they may cancel without finishing, and finds every answer they have already given still there when they come back
Reads the market we inferred and confirms or corrects it — or states it in their own words, where nothing was measured for the domain their account will use
Confirms who they compete with — the suggestions we found, plus any rival they know and we don't, up to five
Chooses whether pages go out on their own and where they publish, then submits the three decisions once
Watches the deep pass run and arrives inside the app — and, where it found less than a month of pages to write, is told that on arrival rather than weeks later

Selects tomorrow's page and reads why it exists — the search it targets, who answers that search today, and what would count as it having worked
Opens the full draft and reads it end to end, checking what it is grounded in, that it sounds like their business, and that it makes no claim they forbid

Fixes a sentence they disagree with, watching the page re-render as they type, closes the tab without saving anything explicitly, and where the edit trips their do-not-claim list is told which entry it matched and edits it again
Approves it, vetoes it, or does nothing at all and lets the veto window run out — and can stop everything in one action if they change their mind

Finds the page live the next morning on their own domain or in their own WordPress, published without their having done anything — or, where something stopped it going out, finds it waiting on them instead of live, with what stopped it named, and sends it out again or drops it for good
